name: es30-normal-mapping
title: Normal mapping: tangent space, specular map, mip chains
summary: Brick wall, rotating crate and sphere lit per fragment by an orbiting point light: procedural albedo, tangent-space normal and specular maps with full mip chains (trilinear), CPU-computed tangents with handedness; validated against an analytic CPU model with negative controls.
spec: ES 3.0 §3.8.1 Texture Objects, §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification
ES 3.0 §3.8.10 Texture Minification (3.8.10.1 level of detail, 3.8.10.2 texel selection, 3.8.10.4 Mipmapping), §3.8.11 Magnification
ES 3.0 §3.8.13 Texture Completeness, §3.9.2 Shader Execution (incomplete textures, MAX_TEXTURE_IMAGE_UNITS)
ES 3.0 §4.1.9 Dithering, §2.1.6.2 float to normalized fixed-point conversion
ES 3.0 §4.4.2.4 Attaching Texture Images to a Framebuffer, §6.1.13 Framebuffer Object Queries
ES 3.0 Tables 6.32 and 6.33 (texture image unit limits)
GLSL ES 3.00 §4.1.7 Opaque Types, §4.5.1 Range and Precision, §4.5.4 Default Precision Qualifiers
GLSL ES 3.00 §5.4.2 Vector and Matrix Constructors, §8.5 Geometric Functions, §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions

api.glGenTextures: three textures (albedo, normal, specular); TEXTURE_BINDING_2D of units 0, 1, 2 equals them
api.glBindTexture: per-unit binding verified with TEXTURE_BINDING_2D; sampled pixels match the CPU model of each map
api.glActiveTexture: units 0, 1, 2 hold the three maps; the lit pixels depend on all three (negative controls fail without them)
api.glTexImage2D: 8 levels x 3 textures (RGBA8, RGBA8, R8) uploaded level by level; every byte read back through a framebuffer object equals the CPU chain
api.glPixelStorei: UNPACK_ALIGNMENT 1: the 2x2 and 1x1 R8 levels (rows of 2 and 1 bytes) read back identical
api.glTexParameteri: MIN_FILTER NEAREST gives the exact CPU texel at 2454 wall probes; LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR at lambda = 1 blends levels 1 and 2; MIN_FILTER read back
api.glGetUniformLocation: all lit-program uniforms located; unused/mislocated uniforms would change the lit colours
api.glUniform1i: sampler units 0/1/2 read back with glGetUniformiv; feature toggles (normal map, specular map, handedness) change the pixels as predicted
api.glUniform1f: ambient and shininess: part of the lit-colour CPU model (max error 0.62/255)
api.glUniform3f: light position/colour and eye: part of the lit-colour CPU model, incl. the animated light of the validated frame
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: model and view-projection matrices: probe pixels land on the analytically projected points
api.glUniformMatrix3fv: normal matrix of the rotated crate: its 369 probes match the CPU model, a model without the rotated tangent frame does not
api.glGenBuffers: vertex and index buffer per mesh
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER and ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER (the latter recorded in the VAO)
api.glBufferData: interleaved position/normal/uv/tangent vertices and 16-bit indices; geometry, UVs and tangents observed through the probes
api.glBindVertexArray: VAO state replays the four attribute arrays and the element buffer
api.glVertexAttribPointer: 4-component tangent with handedness in w, uv, normal, position interleaved; verified by the lit pixels
api.glDrawElements: UNSIGNED_SHORT triangles; wall, crate and sphere
api.glViewport: full-surface viewport: pixel centres map to the CPU-projected ray hits
api.glGenFramebuffers: temporary FBO to read back mip levels
api.glBindFramebuffer: FBO bound for the level readback, default framebuffer restored
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: attaches level 0..7 of each texture (ES 3.0 allows any level); status COMPLETE
api.glReadPixels: lit passes (probe comparison) and mip level readback
api.glUseProgram: lit and marker programs: draws produce the verified colours

visual_review.notes: Viewed the gpu, llvmpipe and zink 256x256 captures (identical to <0.2% MAE), an 800x800 capture and an interactive xvfb session driven by key events. Dark-red brick wall whose bevelled bricks and recessed grey mortar exist only in the normal map; warm light-bulb disc at the upper right with a raking highlight and glints on the glazed bricks while the mortar stays matte; tilted brick crate (left, one face dark = ambient only) and brick sphere (right) with correctly bent bevels. Keys: N flattens the bricks, S makes the mortar glossy, H breaks the right half of the wall (bevels inside out), F bilinear shows aliasing, V shows albedo / blue-violet normal map / specular mask (mirrored about the seam).
